More of the same annotators' work becomes double-rated, without changing what any
judgment means.

Agreement statistics rest entirely on pairs judged independently by two or more people.
The corpus held 107 such pairs and 706 judged exactly once — each of those one signature
away from counting. The second-opinion rate was a fixed 1 request in 5; it is now a
controller aimed at a target share, weighted so that new agreement does not simply
become agreement with whoever has judged most.

Routing decides which pairs are offered. It does not touch the judgment: nobody sees a
pair twice, and nobody ever sees another annotator's answer. Every judgment now records
which strategy served it, and the Admin panel reports Krippendorff's alpha with each
strategy removed — the check that a change in routing collected agreement rather than
manufacturing it.

Also in this release: a per-address rate ceiling separate from the per-account one, so a
seminar room sharing one network address is no longer throttled to forty judgments a
minute between everyone in it; "Judge this!", an invitation to judge one specific pair
that carries no trace of the sender's answer; a human check that speaks Romanian and can
be deferred past the first few judgments without being weakened; and a deploy script
that backs up, health-checks and rolls back on its own.

No corpus release accompanies this one. Under the pre-registered criteria a version is
cut on data volume, and double-rated pairs stand at 107 against a threshold of 185.
